message.abstract: <jats:p>Machine learning models often encounter out-of-distribution (OOD) data, which can significantly reduce model accuracy. This issue is especially critical in fields such as healthcare and autonomous driving. To address it, OOD detection methods were developed to identify semantic shifts, which are samples that do not belong to any of the known in-distribution (ID) categories. However, another type of distribution shift exists: covariate shift, where samples differ in appearance from the known distribution while still belonging to the same categories. Existing OOD detectors are often sensitive to covariate shift, incorrectly flagging such samples as OOD even though they should be correctly classified. To address this limitation, recent research has introduced the concept of Full-Spectrum OOD detection, which aims to detect semantic shift examples while correctly identifying as ID covariate shifted samples. This study presents the first systematic review of this emerging field and introduces new taxonomies for classifying and comparing existing methods. Our review identifies a lack of standardized terminology and evaluation protocols and highlights a predominant focus on far-OOD scenarios in the current literature. Finally, we identified the current challenges and future directions of this subject and provide guidelines to practitioners and researchers to improve the limitations that we detected.</jats:p>
title: Towards Full-Spectrum Out-of-Distribution Detection: Bridging Semantic and Covariate Shift
